about.title: Red Bluff Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a death in Red Bluff comes without warning, the paperwork arrives before the grief has anywhere to go. Tehama County's 2025 public records list 44 injury collisions and 58 people hurt on streets like Main Street, Walnut Street, Antelope Boulevard and Route 36, with one life lost to traffic. California treats a wrongful death claim as a civil matter, entirely separate from whatever the district attorney decides to do. The people allowed to bring it are limited: a spouse or registered domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The clock is generally two years from the date of death, and it shrinks considerably when a city, county, or state agency is involved. What a family may recover includes funeral and burial expenses, the income the person would have provided, and the harder-to-measure loss of love, companionship, and guidance. LawProactive is not a law firm; we connect Red Bluff families, at no cost, with an independent attorney who takes these cases on contingency, so nothing is owed unless there is a recovery.

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney you're matched with can tell you quickly where your family stands.

items.title: The deadline is handled, not guessed
items.desc: Two years from the date of death is the general rule, but a claim involving a public agency has a much shorter window. An independent attorney can identify which applies before time becomes the problem.

items.title: A civil case, on your terms
items.desc: A wrongful death claim proceeds separately from any criminal charges, and it can seek funeral costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love and guidance. Network attorneys work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Does a criminal case have to finish before we can file in Red Bluff?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves on its own track, regardless of what the Tehama County District Attorney does or doesn't pursue. The two cases have different goals and different standards of proof. Many families begin the civil process while a criminal matter is still open.

items.question: Our loss happened on Route 36. Does that change anything?
items.answer: It might. Route 36 is a state highway, and if a public agency's road design or maintenance played any role, California requires a formal claim against that agency far sooner than the usual two years. An attorney can look at the circumstances and confirm which deadline governs. Bringing records in early keeps every option open.

items.question: What can our family actually recover after a wrongful death?
items.answer: California allows recovery for funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have contributed over time, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. The specific amount depends entirely on the facts, and no honest attorney will predict a figure at the outset. Your matched attorney can walk you through how these losses are evaluated.
